To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the fPSA/t PSA ratio improves the diagnostic validity of PSA in the range of 4 to 10 micrograms/l and that the ratio of ACT-PSA/tPS is not superior to the fPSA%/tPSA ratio.
the fPSA/t PSA ratio improves the sensitivity and specificity of the PSA test in prostate cancer diagnosis and that the number of biopsied men can be reduced in this way.
PSA and its derivatives can be used for the early detection of carcinoma of the prostate.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of an improved PSA assay for the diagnosis of prostate cancer.
the development of an improved method of PSA determination and the use of molecular PSA forms for the detection of cancer in patients with PSA levels between 4 and 10 micrograms/l.
the development of new markers for prostate cancer diagnosis and with the validation of new markers in clinical practice.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the use of fPSA in addition to total PSA is the most promising way of improving the diagnostic validity of prostate cancer.
PSA is the only marker that is currently available and that can be recommended in the early diagnosis and in the monitoring and follow-up of patients with prostate cancer.
the fPSA/t ratio is superior to the other molecular PSA forms in terms of sensitivity and specificity for the diagnosis of prostate cancer.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the use of fPSA% and the ratio of fPSAs to ACT-PSA and cPSA improves the specificity and sensitivity in the diagnosis and monitoring of prostate cancer.
fPSA is a useful diagnostic tool for prostate cancer detection, especially in the gray zone of tPSA.
PSA and fPSA are the most useful markers for the diagnosis of prostate cancer.
The main takeaway from our work is that
PSA and hK2 molecular forms have the potential for use in clinical practice.
fPSA% is superior to tPSA and ACT-PSA for the diagnosis of prostate cancer.
the use of PSA forms and derivatives is not yet established in the clinical practice of urology.
